assessments.subtitle: Rotterdam Criteria & Hyperandrogenic Pattern Evaluation
identifiedMarkers: Cyclical cystic jawline breakouts logged in recent entries
negativeMarkers: No hirsutism or excess terminal facial hair reported
physicianDiscussionPoints: Review ovarian ultrasound for polycystic morphology (>12 follicles per ovary).
Assess whether metabolic inositol supplementation is indicated.
Evaluate regular biphasic ovulatory temperature shifts.
assessments.clinicalRationale: Evaluated using the Rotterdam Consensus (requires 2 of 3: oligo/anovulation, clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries). Calculated risk is 38% based on your real cycle variance (±2.5d) and logged skin/metabolic indicators.

assessments.subtitle: Dysmenorrhea Severity & Deep Pelvic Pain Mapping
identifiedMarkers: Non-menstrual pelvic pain reported at severity 2/5
Radiating lower lumbar pain during menstrual phase
recommendedLabTests: Specialized High-Resolution Deep Infiltrating Pelvic Ultrasound
Pelvic MRI with IV Contrast (if deep infiltrative endometriosis suspected)
physicianDiscussionPoints: Differentiate primary dysmenorrhea from secondary endometriosis.
Discuss targeted hormonal management (progestins or combined therapy).
Evaluate non-menstrual pelvic pain or gastrointestinal symptoms during menses.
assessments.clinicalRationale: Endometriosis presents with progressive dysmenorrhea, pelvic soreness, and back radiation. Your logs show peak menses pain of 3/5 and pelvic soreness of 2/5, placing pattern correlation at 68%.

assessments.subtitle: Ovulation Regularity, Cervical Mucus & Luteal Adequacy
identifiedMarkers: Fertile egg-white cervical mucus identified during fertile window
negativeMarkers: Optimal reproductive age window (31 yrs) and regular cycle frequency (29d)
recommendedLabTests: Day 21 (Mid-Luteal) Serum Progesterone (> 10 ng/mL confirms ovulation)
Serum Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) & Ovarian Reserve panel
Thyroid Panel (TSH, Free T4) and Serum Prolactin
physicianDiscussionPoints: Confirm biphasic ovulatory cycles with serum progesterone.
Review preconception methylated folate and vitamin D3 optimization.
Track fertile cervical fluid consistency around mid-cycle.
assessments.clinicalRationale: Analyzes spontaneous ovulatory frequency and luteal phase stability. Evaluated based on age 31, cervical mucus records, and cycle cadence.

assessments.subtitle: Vasomotor, Circadian & Follicular Transition Screening
identifiedMarkers: Zero vasomotor symptoms or transition patterns detected
negativeMarkers: Age 31 is well below standard perimenopausal onset (<40)
No vasomotor instability or night sweats recorded
recommendedLabTests: Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DEXA bone density if indicated)
physicianDiscussionPoints: Discuss non-hormonal and hormonal support if vasomotor flashes arise.
Monitor bone density and cardiovascular lipid panel changes.
Optimize circadian sleep hygiene and strength training.
assessments.clinicalRationale: Assesses neuroendocrine and vasomotor indicators of hormonal transition against current patient age (31) and symptom records.
